Policy instruments: Export licensing, Entity List restrictions and foreign direct product rules
Capabilities affected: Specified advanced computing chips, semiconductor equipment, software and technology
Strategic effect: Can restrict access based on the item, destination, end user and end use
Scope and limitations: Foreign-made items are covered only when jurisdictional tests are met. The January 2026 announcement describes conditional case-by-case review for H200, MI325X and similar chips, not unrestricted sales or a blanket ban on all advanced chips.

Policy instruments: CHIPS and Science Act incentives and research support
Capabilities affected: Domestic fabrication, semiconductor research and advanced packaging
Strategic effect: Encourages domestic investment and supply diversification
Scope and limitations: Awards carry eligibility, performance and national-security conditions. Awarded funding and announced projects are not completed manufacturing capacity.

Policy instruments: National export licensing alongside the EU dual-use framework
Capabilities affected: Specified lithography and other semiconductor manufacturing equipment
Strategic effect: Subjects covered exports to authorization and security review
Scope and limitations: The cited national measure applies to specified exports outside the EU and is not a blanket export ban. Dutch licensing decisions are distinct from any separately applicable U.S. controls.

Policy instruments: Export controls under the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act
Capabilities affected: Specified semiconductor manufacturing equipment and associated technology
Scope and limitations: The 2023 expansion added 23 equipment categories across destinations. Licensing procedures differ by destination and transaction; Japan operates its own legal framework.

Policy instruments: Export licensing and destination- or end-use-specific restrictions
Capabilities affected: Controlled categories of gallium, germanium, graphite and other dual-use materials
Strategic effect: Can constrain access to specified industrial inputs
Dated policy reference: Unified control list: 2024-12-01; U.S.-specific restrictions: 2024-12-03; partial suspension: 2025-11-09 through 2026-11-27
Scope and limitations: Announcement 72 suspended paragraph 2 of Announcement 46, not the entire control system. Product classifications and other controls still matter. These materials serve different semiconductor, optical, power and infrastructure uses.

Policy instruments: Tax incentives, financing and research support
Capabilities affected: Domestic integrated circuits, software and supporting capabilities
Strategic effect: Encourages domestic investment and technological development
Scope and limitations: Program eligibility varies. Support for domestic capability does not establish technological self-sufficiency.

Policy instruments: Industrial support, research programs and cross-strait investment or technical-cooperation review
Capabilities affected: Chip design, advanced processes, packaging and specified overseas activities
Strategic effect: Supports domestic capabilities and subjects covered investments or technical cooperation in mainland China to review
Dated policy reference: Five Trusted Industry Sectors plan approved: 2025-07-08; investment FAQ consulted: 2026-10-24
Scope and limitations: Cross-strait permissions and restrictions depend on the activity and applicable rules. They are not a universal prohibition on overseas fabs or a simple fixed rule for transferring process generations.

Policy instruments: Policy finance, infrastructure support and semiconductor research investment
Capabilities affected: Memory, fabrication, packaging and supplier capabilities
Scope and limitations: Programs differ in eligibility and implementation schedule. This dated example is not an inventory of every subsequent incentive.

Policy instruments: European Chips Act, research programs and member-state support
Capabilities affected: Semiconductor research, pilot lines, production and ecosystem resilience
Strategic effect: Expands regional capabilities and addresses selected dependencies
Dated policy reference: Chips Act in force: 2023-09-21; Chips Act 2.0 proposed: 2026-06
Scope and limitations: An enacted framework, a legislative proposal and individual funding approvals have different status. National schemes also remain subject to applicable EU rules.

Policy instruments: Semicon India incentives, design support and semiconductor mission programs
Capabilities affected: Fabrication, packaging, chip design and supporting supply chains
Strategic effect: Seeks to attract investment and build domestic capabilities
Scope and limitations: The update distinguishes approved projects from production and describes India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 as a budget announcement. Delivery requires equipment, skills and customer qualification.

Jurisdiction: Saudi Arabia and United Arab Emirates
Policy instruments: State-backed investment, infrastructure programs and technology partnerships
Capabilities affected: AI compute, data centers, cloud services and models
Strategic effect: Finances domestic AI capacity and international partnerships
Dated policy reference: HUMAIN launch: 2025-05-12; UAE-U.S. AI campus announcement: 2025-05
Scope and limitations: These are separate national initiatives. Announced capacity depends on construction, power, financing and applicable technology-access approvals.
